glossary.distension: Swelling of the abdomen from trapped gas or fluid.
glossary.dehydration: Loss of more body water than is taken in.
glossary.electrolyte disturbance: Abnormal blood levels of salts such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.colicky pain: Pain that comes and goes in waves.
glossary.Crohn's disease: Inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gut and cause strictures.
glossary.cardinal signs: The key features that define a condition.
glossary.colorectal cancer: Cancer of the colon or rectum.
glossary.diverticular stricture: Narrowing of the colon from scarring after repeated diverticulitis.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.opioids: Strong painkillers, such as morphine, that slow gut movement.
glossary.rigid abdomen: A board-like hard abdomen, a sign of peritonitis.
glossary.percussion tenderness: Pain when the abdomen is tapped, a sign of peritoneal irritation.
glossary.peritonitis: Inflammation of the peritoneum, the lining of the abdomen.
glossary.ischaemia: Too little blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.tachycardia: Heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.double wall sign: Both sides of the bowel wall visible on X-ray because free air lies outside it.
glossary.air-fluid levels: Flat lines on an erect X-ray where gas sits on top of fluid in dilated bowel.
glossary.pigmented lesions: Darkly coloured spots, here on lips, mouth, palms and soles.
glossary.plantar: On the sole of the foot.
glossary.acute abdomen: Sudden severe abdominal pain that may need urgent surgery.
glossary.CT abdomen and pelvis: Cross-sectional scan showing the site and cause of the obstruction.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: kidney function, sodium and potassium.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.sigmoidoscope: Camera tube passed into the rectum and sigmoid colon.
glossary.decompression: Releasing trapped gas and fluid to reduce pressure in the bowel.
glossary.motility: The bowel's ability to move its contents along.
glossary.peristalsis: Waves of muscle contraction that push bowel contents forward.
glossary.enteric nervous system: The network of nerves in the gut wall that coordinates peristalsis.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the bowel wall.
glossary.faecal peritonitis: Peritonitis from faeces leaking into the abdomen; very serious.
glossary.oedema: Swelling from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.electrolyte derangement: Abnormal salt levels in the blood from fluid losses.
glossary.venous congestion: Blood backing up because the veins are blocked.
glossary.arterial occlusion: Blockage of an artery so blood cannot reach the tissue.
glossary.femoral hernia: Hernia through the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament; high strangulation risk.
glossary.incarceration: A hernia stuck and unable to be pushed back.
glossary.hernia: Protrusion of an organ or tissue through a weak spot in its containing wall.
glossary.tumour: An abnormal growth of tissue, benign or malignant.
glossary.dilatation: Widening or stretching of a hollow organ.
